cohort: The study included 200 mothers (mean age 24.32 years) who had undergone either normal vaginal delivery or caesarean section at a government tertiary care hospital in Bengaluru.
finding: Normal vaginal delivery was associated with quicker physical recuperation and higher mean scores in the physical health domain of quality of life compared to caesarean section.
mod_finding: Normal vaginal delivery was associated with a quicker physical recuperation compared to caesarean section, which demanded a longer recovery period and potential physical limitations.
cross-section timing: After delivery, specific timing not mentioned.
